strategies.name: Test with nofpclass(all) attribute
strategies.target: SimplifyDemandedUseFPClass optimization when all floating-point classes are forbidden
strategies.rationale: When a function has nofpclass(all) attribute, all floating-point classes are forbidden. The optimization returns poison for any non-undef return value. This might be too aggressive and could change observable behavior.
strategies.expected_issue: The optimization replaces valid (though contract-violating) code with poison, potentially changing program behavior.

strategies.name: Test select instruction with contradictory constraints
strategies.rationale: When analyzing a select in a function with nofpclass attribute, if one operand is known to never satisfy the demanded mask (i.e., always violates the function's constraints), the optimization returns the other operand. But this assumes the violating operand can exist, which contradicts the function's attributes.
strategies.expected_issue: The optimization might return the wrong value when one operand violates function constraints.

strategies.name: Test computeKnownFPClass without function context
strategies.target: computeKnownFPClass function's handling of function return attributes
strategies.rationale: computeKnownFPClass doesn't consider function return attributes when analyzing values inside the function. This could lead to incorrect analysis when values are constrained by the function's nofpclass attribute.
strategies.expected_issue: Incorrect analysis of floating-point classes for values inside functions with nofpclass attributes.

197 /// Legal integers and common types are considered desirable. This is used to
198 /// avoid creating instructions with types that may not be supported well by the
199 /// the backend.
200 /// NOTE: This treats i8, i16 and i32 specially because they are common
201 ///       types in frontend languages.
202 bool InstCombinerImpl::isDesirableIntType(unsigned BitWidth) const {
203   switch (BitWidth) {
204   case 8:
205   case 16:
206   case 32:
207     return true;
208   default:
209     return DL.isLegalInteger(BitWidth);
210   }
211 }

213 /// Return true if it is desirable to convert an integer computation from a
214 /// given bit width to a new bit width.
215 /// We don't want to convert from a legal or desirable type (like i8) to an
216 /// illegal type or from a smaller to a larger illegal type. A width of '1'
217 /// is always treated as a desirable type because i1 is a fundamental type in
218 /// IR, and there are many specialized optimizations for i1 types.
219 /// Common/desirable widths are equally treated as legal to convert to, in
220 /// order to open up more combining opportunities.
221 bool InstCombinerImpl::shouldChangeType(unsigned FromWidth,
222                                         unsigned ToWidth) const {
223   bool FromLegal = FromWidth == 1 || DL.isLegalInteger(FromWidth);
224   bool ToLegal = ToWidth == 1 || DL.isLegalInteger(ToWidth);
225 
226   // Convert to desirable widths even if they are not legal types.
227   // Only shrink types, to prevent infinite loops.
228   if (ToWidth < FromWidth && isDesirableIntType(ToWidth))
229     return true;
230 
231   // If this is a legal or desiable integer from type, and the result would be
232   // an illegal type, don't do the transformation.
233   if ((FromLegal || isDesirableIntType(FromWidth)) && !ToLegal)
234     return false;
235 
236   // Otherwise, if both are illegal, do not increase the size of the result. We
237   // do allow things like i160 -> i64, but not i64 -> i160.
238   if (!FromLegal && !ToLegal && ToWidth > FromWidth)
239     return false;
240 
241   return true;
242 }

test_traj.arguments:
{"test":["```llvm
; Test case demonstrating issue with SimplifyDemandedUseFPClass
; when function has nofpclass(all) attribute

define nofpclass(all) float @contradictory_function(float %x) {
  ; Function promises to never return any floating-point value
  ; but returns %x which is a float
  ; This is contradictory - the function contract is violated
  ret float %x
}
```","opt -S -passes="instcombine" report_test.ll -o report_test_opt.ll"],"thoughts":"Bug Triggering Analysis:
The test case triggers the SimplifyDemandedUseFPClass optimization in visitReturnInst. The function has nofpclass(all) attribute, which forbids all floating-point classes. When visitReturnInst is called:
1. It gets the return attribute: ReturnClass = fcAllFlags (all classes forbidden)
2. It computes DemandedMask = ~ReturnClass = fcNone (empty set)
3. It calls SimplifyDemandedUseFPClass(RetVal, fcNone, ...)
4. SimplifyDemandedUseFPClass checks if DemandedMask == fcNone (line 1908)
5. Since RetVal (%x) is not undef, it returns PoisonValue::get(VTy) (line 1909)
6. visitReturnInst creates a new return instruction with poison

This transformation is technically correct according to LLVM semantics (contract violation is undefined behavior), but it changes observable behavior. The original code would return the float value %x (which violates the contract), while the optimized code returns poison. This could affect program behavior in ways the programmer didn't expect.

Fix Weakness Analysis:
The weakness in the fix is that it enables an optimization without proper handling of edge cases:
1. The optimization doesn't consider whether replacing contract-violating code with poison is desirable
2. The optimization assumes computeKnownFPClass has complete information about floating-point class constraints, but it doesn't propagate function return attributes to values inside the function
3. The select instruction optimization has logic that could return the wrong operand when dealing with contradictory constraints

The patch removes the safety flag (EnableSimplifyDemandedUseFPClass) that was guarding this optimization, exposing these issues in production code."}
